paper.title: Robust Budget Pacing with a Single Sample

settings.name_in_paper: Online allocation with a single resource (budget pacing) with one sample per distribution
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Online resource allocation / budget pacing where the request (reward and consumption functions) is observed before acting; not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Requests drawn independently from unknown time-varying distributions P_t (not identical, not adversarial); environment mapping is approximate
Learner has one sample per period from sampling distributions tilde P_t, possibly different from P_t; regret degrades with total Wasserstein distance
Benchmark is the fluid-optimal value FLUID({P_t}) under a budget B
Rewards f(x) <= kappa b(x), f <= f_bar, b <= b_bar; general position assumption
settings.definition_quote: The request $\gamma_t$ at time $t$ is drawn from a distribution $\PP_t \in \Delta(\S)$ unknown to the decision maker, independently of the requests at other time steps... we focus on the setting where the decision maker has access to one independent sample $\tilde \gamma_t \sim \tilde \PP_t$ for each $t \in [T]$.

algorithms.name: Learning the Dual and Earning with It (Static Dual Policy)
Dual FTRL with Target Rate Estimation

symbols.kappa: upper bound on reward-to-consumption ratio f(x) <= kappa b(x)
symbols.b_bar: upper bound on per-request resource consumption

conditions: sampling distributions equal request distributions (tilde P_t = P_t)

source.label: thm:learned-dual-regret
source.quote: If $\PP_t = \tilde \PP_t$ for all $t \in [T]$, then Algorithm~\ref{alg:learned-dual} (denoted by $A$) satisfies $\regret(A) \leq  12 \kappa \bar b + 2 \kappa r(T)$.

results.notes: Regret = FLUID - E[reward], fluid benchmark; quantity marked other. r(T) substituted from Theorem 1.

bound.expression_latex: C_1 \sqrt{T \log(T)} + C_2 \sum_{t=1}^T \W(\PP_t, \tilde \PP_t),\ C_1 = \frac{12 \bar b^2 \sqrt{d_R}}{\sigma} +  \sqrt{d_R} + 12 \kappa \bar b,\ C_2 = 2(1+\kappa)

symbols.b_bar: upper bound on per-request resource consumption
symbols.sigma_h: strong convexity parameter of the regularizer h
symbols.W_total: sum_t Wasserstein distance W(P_t, tilde P_t)

conditions: one sample per period from tilde P_t

source.label: thm:main-result
source.quote: Let $A$ be Algorithm~\ref{alg:dual-descent} with target sequence $\{\lambda_t\}_t$, where $\lambda_t = \tilde b_t^*(\tilde \mu)$ ..., regularizer $h(\cdot)$ and step-size $\eta = \sqrt{d_R/ T}$... Then, $\regret(A) \leq C_1 \sqrt{T \log(T)} + C_2 \sum_{t=1}^T \W(\PP_t, \tilde \PP_t)$ where $C_1 = \frac{12 \bar b^2 \sqrt{d_R}}{\sigma} +  \sqrt{d_R} + 12 \kappa \bar b$ and $C_2 = 2(1+\kappa)$.

results.notes: Fluid-benchmark regret in expectation. Theorem 3 (general regret decomposition R1+R2+R3) not recorded separately.
